key_insight: RECONTEXT shows that long-context reasoning can be improved without retraining the model by repeatedly replaying the most relevant evidence, helping the LLM actually use information it already has access to. In simple terms: it closes the gap between “can read long inputs” and “can reason over them.”
problem_solved: LLMs often accept very long prompts but still miss or underuse important supporting evidence buried in the context. This paper addresses the challenge of making models reliably extract and leverage relevant information across long documents or conversations.
method: Training-free inference harness that wraps around an existing LLM.
Recursively replays key evidence back into the model to reinforce relevant context.
Focuses the model on supporting passages instead of relying on a single-pass reading of the full input.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a practical way to boost long-context performance without expensive fine-tuning or architecture changes. It can improve tasks like document QA, multi-hop reasoning, and long conversation understanding using existing LLMs.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing long input → evidence selection → recursive replay → improved answer.

paper_title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
paper_authors: Yanjun Zhao, Ruizhong Qiu, Tianxin Wei, Yuanchen Bei, Zhining Liu
